Regrowth after partial hepatectomy

A healthy adult undergoes removal of part of the liver. During recovery, growth signals induce surviving hepatocytes to enter the cell cycle, increasing the number of viable cells in the remnant. Which process chiefly restores cell number?

  1. Squamous metaplasia
  2. Coagulative necrosis
  3. Disuse atrophy
  4. Dystrophic calcification
  5. Compensatory hyperplasia
Answer and explanation

Compensatory hyperplasia

Hepatocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and proliferate in response to growth signals after tissue loss.

Option explanations

Compensatory hyperplasia: Hepatocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and proliferate in response to growth signals after tissue loss.

Squamous metaplasia: Squamous metaplasia would change epithelial phenotype rather than restore hepatocyte number.

Coagulative necrosis: Necrosis decreases viable tissue mass.

Disuse atrophy: Disuse atrophy reduces cell size and organ mass.

Dystrophic calcification: Calcification deposits calcium rather than replacing functional cells.

Related lecture

Cellular Adaptations (Growth Adaptations): Hypertrophy, Hyperplasia, Atrophy, Metaplasia
